passage:
'Arre, why is Noor crying?'
'Her balloon popped, Rajni. Look at her.'
'Oh no. Come, Noor, come to me.'
'Rajni, look at Jassi now.'
'Jassi? Why are you crying, baby? Your balloon is fine!'
Jasleen, two, held her red balloon tight. Her lip wobbled, then she wailed too, looking at Noor.
'Nothing happened to you, Jassi.'
'She heard Noor,' said Bebe. 'Babies catch it like yawns. Pick her up.'

qa.q: What happened to Noor's balloon?
qa.a: Noor's balloon popped.

qa.q: Why did Jasleen start to cry even though her balloon was fine?
qa.a: She was upset by hearing and seeing Noor cry, so she felt the sadness too without knowing why.

qa.q: What could Rajni do to help Jasleen right then?
qa.a: Rajni could pick Jasleen up as Bebe said and hold her close so she feels safe again.

qa.q: How does Bebe explain Jasleen's tears?
qa.a: Bebe sees it as natural: Jasleen heard Noor, and babies catch crying like yawns.

grounding: Shows a two-year-old at a family gathering who starts crying on hearing another toddler cry, without any reason of her own.

passage:
Note from Nilesh, room teacher, Little Steps nursery, Tuesday:
At drop-off, Mia cried hard when her dad left. Tarun was stacking blocks happily nearby. He stopped, stared at Mia, and his face crumpled. Soon he was crying too, then two more children. None of them had any reason of their own. I sat on the mat, picked up Mia, and hummed our bus song. Tarun crawled over and leaned on my knee. Within a few minutes the room was quiet again 🙂

qa.q: What was Tarun doing before Mia started crying?
qa.a: Tarun was stacking blocks happily nearby.

qa.q: What does Tarun's face crumpling as he stared at Mia suggest?
qa.a: It suggests Mia's crying upset him and he began to feel the same distress, even though nothing had happened to him.

qa.q: How did Nilesh help the room calm down, and why did it work?
qa.a: Nilesh sat on the mat, held Mia and hummed the bus song, which calmed Mia and drew Tarun in, so the calm spread like the crying had.

qa.q: What was drop-off like for the other children in the room?
qa.a: Two more children started crying too, so for them it was a sudden sad moment that none of them could explain.

grounding: A nursery teacher's note records how one toddler's crying spread to others who had no reason of their own.

passage: At the anganwadi in the village, the children sat on a mat eating chana. Suddenly a goat bleated loudly at the door and little Faiz burst into tears. Dilnaz, two, stopped chewing. She looked at Faiz. Her eyes went wide and her chin began to shake. Then she was crying too, and so was the boy beside her. Zeenat didi laughed softly, pulled all three onto her lap and sang the rain song until the sobbing stopped.

qa.q: What made Faiz burst into tears?
qa.a: A goat bleated loudly at the door.

qa.q: How can you tell Dilnaz was starting to feel upset?
qa.a: She stopped chewing, her eyes went wide and her chin began to shake as she looked at Faiz.

qa.q: What did Zeenat didi do well to calm the children?
qa.a: She pulled all three onto her lap and sang the rain song, giving them comfort together instead of scolding.

qa.q: Why might the boy beside Dilnaz have started crying?
qa.a: He probably caught the sadness from Faiz and Dilnaz crying next to him, not because of anything that happened to him.

grounding: Shows toddlers at a village anganwadi catching crying from one another after one child is startled.

passage: At the library's toddler morning in Lisbon, Priscila, two, dropped her biscuit and wailed. Freya, beside her with a shape sorter, froze. She stared at Priscila's red face. Her own lip wobbled, and then she was crying too, loud and hard, with no biscuit trouble at all. Across the rug, a baby boy stopped clapping and crawled fast to his papa. Freya's mum scooped up both girls and hummed. Slowly the sobs became hiccups.

qa.q: What did Priscila drop?
qa.a: Her biscuit.

qa.q: Why did Freya start crying when nothing had happened to her?
qa.a: She saw Priscila's red face and heard the wail, and the upset seemed to pass straight to her without her knowing why.

qa.q: How did Freya's mum help the crying settle?
qa.a: She scooped up both girls and hummed, giving them a calm, steady feeling to settle into.

qa.q: How might the baby boy across the rug have felt?
qa.a: He seemed worried by the crying, stopping his clapping and crawling fast to his papa for comfort.

grounding: One toddler's crying spreads to another who cries without knowing why, and a nearby baby looks worried.

passage: I'm Suraj, and I help at my aunt's daycare after college. Yesterday at nap time, little Aarush woke and cried for his mother. Preeti, one and a half, sat straight up on the next mat and stared at him. Her face crumpled. Then she was crying too, big tears, though nothing had happened to her. A toddler in the corner joined in. My aunt put on a slow lullaby and sat down among the mats, patting backs.

qa.q: What did Aarush cry for?
qa.a: For his mother.

qa.q: Why might Preeti have started crying though nothing had happened to her?
qa.a: Seeing Aarush upset right beside her seems to have made her feel upset too, the feeling spreading before she could know why.

qa.q: Why was the aunt's calm response a good choice?
qa.a: A slow lullaby and gentle patting gave the children a calm feeling to catch instead of more crying.

qa.q: What might nap time have looked like to Suraj, watching the crying spread?
qa.a: Suraj saw one child cry and others join in within moments, which likely felt puzzling and a little overwhelming.

grounding: A daycare helper watches one toddler's crying spread to others who cry without knowing why.

passage:
"Ow! Waaah!" Anirban had bumped his head on the table.
Aadhya stopped stacking cups. She stared at him. Her lip wobbled. "Waaah!"
"Arre, Aadhya, you're not hurt, are you?" Mummy asked, picking her up.
"Ani cry," Aadhya sobbed, pointing.
"Yes, Ani is crying. Mami is holding Ani now. See?"
Aadhya hiccuped, watching Anirban on his mother's lap. Then she held out a cup to him.

qa.q: What did Anirban bump his head on?
qa.a: He bumped his head on the table.

qa.q: Why did Aadhya start crying though she wasn't hurt?
qa.a: Seeing and hearing Anirban cry made her upset and worried too; his distress spread to her.

qa.q: What did Mummy do that helped Aadhya settle?
qa.a: She picked Aadhya up, named what was happening and showed her Ani being held.

qa.q: How might Anirban's mother see Aadhya's tears?
qa.a: She may see them as a sign of how quickly little ones catch each other's feelings, not as a second injury.

grounding: Shows a toddler bursting into tears simply because another small child is crying, without knowing why.

passage:
Creche note, Diwali week. Kavitha, room caregiver.
A cracker burst outside during snack time. Avni jumped and began to cry. Within a minute three other toddlers were crying or staring at her with worried faces; none of them had looked at the window.
I sat on the mat, took Avni on my lap and hummed our tidy-up song. The others crawled close. Soon they were quiet again.
This week we will draw the curtains and play soft music during cracker hours.

qa.q: What happened outside during snack time?
qa.a: A cracker burst outside.

qa.q: What were the other toddlers feeling when Avni began to cry?
qa.a: They felt worried and upset, catching Avni's distress though none of them had noticed the noise.

qa.q: What could help the room during cracker hours this week?
qa.a: Drawing the curtains and playing soft music, as Kavitha planned, and staying calm and close when one child cries.

qa.q: What was it like for Avni when the cracker burst?
qa.a: It was sudden and frightening; being held and hearing a familiar song helped her feel safe again.

grounding: A caregiver's festival-week note shows one toddler's crying spreading to others who did not know what had upset her.

passage:
It was harvest week, and every mother in the village was out in the paddy fields. At the anganwadi, little Lakshmi watched her Amma walk away down the mud path and let out a long wail.
Across the mat, a boy with a rattle stopped shaking it. His face crumpled. Then two more toddlers joined in, looking around, not knowing why.
Manjula, the helper, scooped Lakshmi up and sat down among them, clapping softly and singing the harvest song. One by one the cries turned into sniffles.

qa.q: Where were the mothers during harvest week?
qa.a: Every mother in the village was out in the paddy fields.

qa.q: What was the boy with the rattle feeling when Lakshmi wailed?
qa.a: He felt upset and uneasy, catching Lakshmi's sadness without knowing why she cried.

qa.q: How did Manjula help the whole group settle?
qa.a: She held Lakshmi and sat among all of them, clapping softly and singing, so calm could spread instead.

qa.q: How might Lakshmi's Amma feel if she heard the crying from the path?
qa.a: She might feel torn and worried, needing to work in the fields yet wanting to comfort her child.

grounding: Shows one toddler's wail at a village anganwadi spreading to other toddlers who do not know why they are crying.

passage:
It was snowing outside the Berlin nursery. Inside, the toddlers played on the warm mat.
Jana dropped her cup and began to wail. Felix, beside her, stopped stacking blocks. His lip trembled. Then he cried too.
A third toddler looked at them, confused, and started crying as well.
The carer picked Jana up and hummed a song. Slowly Jana quieted. Felix watched her, sniffed and went back to his blocks.

qa.q: What did Jana drop?
qa.a: Jana dropped her cup.

qa.q: Why did Felix cry even though nothing happened to him?
qa.a: He caught Jana's upset feeling, so he felt upset and scared too without knowing why.

qa.q: How did the carer help the crying spread stop?
qa.a: The carer calmed Jana first with a song, and as Jana quieted, the others settled too.

qa.q: What is it like for the third toddler when the others cry?
qa.a: The third toddler feels confused and upset, crying without knowing what was wrong.

grounding: Shows one toddler crying in a snowy-season nursery and others crying too without knowing why, emotion spreading quickly.

passage:
Monday, rainy: At the creche, thunder boomed. Ritu cried. Yash, playing nearby, stared, then cried too.
Wednesday, still raining: Ritu fell and cried. Yash's face crumpled at once, and he ran to the teacher.
Friday: Thunder again. Ritu started to cry. The teacher sat between them, calm and smiling, and said, "Big noise! We're safe." Yash looked at the teacher's face, not Ritu's. He didn't cry.

qa.q: What made Ritu cry on Monday?
qa.a: Thunder boomed.

qa.q: Why did Yash's face crumple when Ritu fell?
qa.a: He caught Ritu's upset and felt scared and sad too.

qa.q: What did the teacher do on Friday that helped?
qa.a: The teacher sat between them calmly and smiled, so Yash picked up the teacher's calm instead of Ritu's fear.

qa.q: How might Ritu feel when the teacher says "We're safe"?
qa.a: Ritu may feel comforted and less scared, hearing a calm voice nearby.

grounding: Shows a toddler catching another's crying across several rainy days, until a calm adult gives him a different feeling to catch.

passage:
It was Diwali week, and a firecracker burst outside the Delhi daycare. Preeti jumped and burst into tears, clutching her doll.
Jatin, holding a toy car, looked at her. His mouth wobbled. He began to cry too. Two more toddlers joined in.
Nobody knew why they were crying except Preeti.
The caregiver sat on the floor, pulled Preeti close and said softly, "Loud bang. All gone now." Jatin crawled over and leaned on the caregiver's arm. Soon the room was quiet again.

qa.q: What burst outside the daycare?
qa.a: A firecracker burst outside the daycare.

qa.q: Why did Jatin start crying?
qa.a: He saw Preeti crying and caught her fear, feeling upset without knowing why.

qa.q: How did the caregiver calm the room?
qa.a: By sitting down, holding Preeti and speaking softly, the caregiver's calm spread to the others.

qa.q: What is it like for Preeti after the caregiver holds her?
qa.a: Preeti feels safer and comforted, and her calm helps the others settle.

grounding: Shows a toddler's fright at a festival firecracker spreading to others who cry without knowing why.

passage: "Merry Christmas, everyone!" The cousins crowded the living room. A balloon popped. Joseph's lip wobbled, and he wailed. Across the rug, little Wasim stopped stacking cups and stared at Joseph. His face crumpled too. "Why is Wasim crying?" Aunty asked. "He didn't even hear the pop." "He heard Joseph," said Mama, scooping up both boys. "Shh, shh." Joseph sniffled into her shoulder. Wasim watched him, then sniffled too.

qa.q: What popped?
qa.a: A balloon popped.

qa.q: Why did Wasim's face crumple?
qa.a: He seemed upset and worried just from seeing and hearing Joseph cry, even though he didn't know about the pop.

qa.q: What did Mama do that helped?
qa.a: She scooped up both boys together and soothed them, calming the shared distress.

qa.q: How might Aunty see Wasim's crying?
qa.a: Aunty is puzzled, since Wasim didn't hear the pop, not realising crying spreads between little ones.

grounding: Illustrates one toddler's crying spreading to another who does not know the cause.

passage: Nursery note, Monday. At drop-off, Mohit clung to the gate and cried hard. Within a minute, two toddlers near the blocks stopped playing. One began to whimper; the other looked around with a worried face. Neither knew why. Mohit's big sister Reena, who had brought him, looked unsure. "Did I upset them?" I told her no. We sat Mohit on the mat with a picture book and sang softly. The whimpering faded as Mohit calmed. Reena smiled, relieved.

qa.q: Where did Mohit cling while crying?
qa.a: To the gate.

qa.q: What did the two toddlers near the blocks seem to feel?
qa.a: They seemed worried and upset, catching Mohit's distress without knowing why.

qa.q: What helped all the children settle?
qa.a: Calming Mohit with a picture book and soft singing, which eased the others as well.

qa.q: How did Reena feel watching the other toddlers react?
qa.a: She felt unsure and a little guilty at first, then relieved when they calmed.

grounding: Shows a toddler's crying spreading to others at nursery who do not know why.

passage: At the village anganwadi, the ceiling fan stopped with a clank. Hafsa jumped and began to cry. Her cousin Kishore, sitting beside her on the mat, looked at her face, then puckered up and cried too. Soon a third child was whimpering. Their older cousin, waiting by the door, laughed softly. "Kishore, you weren't even scared!" The helper picked up Hafsa and swayed. As she quieted, Kishore quieted too.

qa.q: What made the clank?
qa.a: The ceiling fan stopped with a clank.

qa.q: What does Kishore puckering up suggest about how he felt?
qa.a: It suggests he felt upset and worried just from seeing Hafsa cry, not from the noise.

qa.q: What did the helper do that calmed both children?
qa.a: She picked up Hafsa and swayed, and as Hafsa quieted, Kishore did too.

qa.q: How does the older cousin react to the crying?
qa.a: The older cousin finds it gently funny, noticing that Kishore wasn't even scared.

grounding: Illustrates how one toddler's crying makes another toddler cry without knowing why.

passage: At the nursery in Copenhagen, Freya's mum waved goodbye and Freya began to wail. Mina stopped stacking cups. Her chin wobbled. She looked at Freya, then at the door, and started crying too, though her own papa was still kneeling beside her. A boy by the window joined in. Mina's big brother Oskar, six, stared at them all. 'Nobody left you,' he said, puzzled, and held out her favourite red cup. Mina sniffed, took it, and leaned against his knee.

qa.q: What was Mina doing before Freya started to cry?
qa.a: Mina was stacking cups.

qa.q: Why did Mina start crying even though her papa was still there?
qa.a: Hearing Freya wail made Mina feel worried and sad too; she caught the upset without any reason of her own.

qa.q: How could a nursery teacher help when crying spreads like this?
qa.a: Comfort Freya calmly and quickly, and offer the others a familiar toy or a lap, the way Oskar offered the red cup.

qa.q: Why might Oskar be puzzled by Mina's tears?
qa.a: At six, Oskar looks for a reason, and nobody left Mina, so he doesn't see that her crying simply spread from Freya.

grounding: Shows one toddler's crying in a nursery spreading to others who become upset without knowing why.
